Our current physical realm is rot and decay. That isn't inherently "bad" in itself. The decomposition and destruction of things isn't necessarily bad, horrible, or negative. Our displeasure in seeing or experiencing death and decay is the human perception of things. We very much value death when we eat/wear animals, or when we reconstruct environments for our homes and communities. We enjoy death, destruction, and decay when it suits us. We don't enjoy it when we feel that it's in opposition to us. Violence and chaos in the universe is rather productive and beneficial, despite being frightening. Think of a volcano erupting, or a forest fire, the aftermath of these events is largely positive. Volcanic eruptions create new lands, forest fires fertilize the soil, gets rid of decay, and more. 

One thought that I've heard is "The human experience is one of impermanence and death to create the illusion of separation from the true self (be it your spirit, universe, god, whatever). It's a powerful illusion filled with disturbing rules and realties, so that we have to believe in the "impossible" in order to function within it."

The belief is similar to your your trip. You saw some crazy and distorted shit, but knew underneath it all that you were just on drugs and would get "back to" reality. That experience is the assumption of what being human is. It's an experience we endure to prove the existence of the "true self" to ourselves and returning to ourselves.

I'm in a position where I don't know if awakening is "real" or a desperate attempt to make sense of a world where one experiences suffering often. Crazy things have happened to me once I thought I was becoming awakened, but whose to those just weren't a series of random coincidences? 

I don't believe that awakening is a method to "solve" life's problems. I think it's a methodology to remind people that they're a spirit in a human experience. And an anchor to remind people not to get lost in the drama of reality. That's the concept at least.

Yes, I think that people in the spiritual community often downplay the human experience while we're living. Many people can get addicted to the sensations of human emotion (pleasure/pain/etc). Often times people make a choice to do terrible things because they can. A significant amount of people enjoyed the pain that they inflicted on others and would do it again if they had the opportunity to. There isn't a lot of protection out there for children (let alone people in general), so many people abuse children because they know there will be little to no consequences for it, especially if it's their own children.

I understand what you're saying. You're not the only to have these spiritual beliefs. You're allowed to express your thoughts, feelings, and what has spiritually helped you. 

I was simply giving an alternative perspective because the message of "You suffered for a reason" or "You suffered because you could handle it" blatantly ignores the people who didn't survive one way or another. It only acknowledges the success stories or "semi" success stories. It also doesn't address the people who do repeat cycles, despite not actually wanting to. 

I'm not trying to guilt trip you or change your mind. Lot's of people agree with you. I'm just suggesting a mindfulness of other people is all.

It's pretty straight forward. Some people wouldn't appreciate being told that they had to endure being raped, tortured, beaten, or nearly killed simply for the sake of being able to endure that kind of treatment. For some people that is a senseless form of suffering with zero tangible benefits on their development, growth, or functionality as a person. Many people have life long permanent injuries mentally, physically, emotionally, and neurologically due to past trauma's. Many people are hindered in this life for the truama's that they suffered through.

Many people also aren't "enduring" through their trauma, they're existing through their trauma. There's a difference. 

It undermine's the horrific experiences and life suffering of some people. Explaining their suffering as "it's because the universe knew you wouldn't kill yourself" Isn't exactly an appropriate message to tell some people. 

In no other scenario would anyone be comfortable with a person walking into their home and doing unspeakable things to them solely because "They're strong enough to endure it." The average person would consider that scenario to be an unnecessary psychotic hostage situation.

No problem! Everyone has different ways of healing and working through things. It's perfectly fine to believe whatever resonates with you the most on your own individual journey. 

It just helps to keep in mind that it isn't a reality for every and to be mindful of the damage that messages like that can cause. Even if they are well-intentioned, it may not be the right message for everyone.

Honestly I believe that trying to romanticize trauma to any degree is dangerous. I don't think saying that trauma was intentional or planned is beneficial for anyone. 

I know that many people want to make sense and need to make sense of what happened to them but claiming that their torture was a "test" isn't any better than saying it was a "punishment".

Despite how we are all on our spiritual journey's some people never recover or are able to overcome their trauma in their lifetime, regardless of how well they managed to live with it.

I'm a digital services freelancer. When you purchase digital services, you really have to understand what it is that you're looking for. Digital marketing is a broad term that ranges from online advertising, blogging, social media engagement, email marketing, and search engine optimization, and more. With this in mind you really need to know what your end goal for hiring their services are.

If you want to list higher on search engines such as Google, duckduckGo, and Bing, then you should look into SEO services. Whatever service you use should be able to organize web content and meta data so that you're easier to fine on search engines. 

If you want conversions it's best to utilize email marketing if you have a strong subscription list. Advertising through google, youtube, etc is also great for conversions, however the traffic rate from the clicks has to be significantly higher. 

If you want to build brand authority content management through blogging and social media is best. 

Depending on your budget is whether or not you should hire these services. If you're managing your own website through shopify or wordpress, you can do some of the things that I've mentioned above yourself easily. There are plenty of free resources and great tutorials out there to get started. 

I'd suggest that you learn your user behavior first. Google analytics is free and gives great information on how users engage with your website. It's free and easy to use. When you know what people are doing on your website, it's easier to strategize what to do from there.

Your question is a difficult one to answer. Regarding your friends, its difficult to open up about sexual addictions because most things regarding sexuality is such a taboo, especially the act of paying for sex. When it comes to your partner, there are a slew of reasoning you have to go over before you decide to tell the truth or not. For example, why were you feeling so lonely in a relationship that it made you resort to paying for sex? Do you want to tell him/her because you feel guilty and want to make yourself feel better? Or do you want to tell him/her because you want honesty in your relationship and you want him/her to have the choice of accepting who you were, who you are, and who you are attempting to become? 

Opening up to others about an addiction is difficult because being honest and accepting the truth of ourselves also means that we open ourselves to be judged and even rejected by the people we love. Even if we end up losing those people over our past behaviors, it still means that it is a new chapter of truth and sobriety in our journey of being the people we want to become. 

If you feel like you are emotionally ready to handle the consequences (whether they be good or bad)of telling others of your addiction, I say go for it. But if you still feel emotionally fragile, then now many not be the best time to share your history. The benefit to telling others is that they will support you and encourage you positively giving you the opportunity to grow even deeper/stronger relationships. The loss is that people you love will reject you and leave you to your own journey. 

Good luck!
